strategies.overview: Sandaconda is a good defensive Pokemon in SV ZU thanks to its bulk and Shed Skin. The increased reliability of Rest as recovery lends Sandaconda the longevity to check Pokemon like Muk and Passimian. Options like Stealth Rock, Glare, and Coil diversify Sandaconda into a great support Pokemon or a bulky setup sweeper. Sandaconda is an excellent Terastallization user to boot, enhancing its defensive profile to become even tougher to break or enabling its own sweeps. However, Shed Skin does not make Rest perfectly reliable, hampering Sandaconda's consistency. Physical attackers with super effective STAB moves like Glastrier and Virizion are very problematic for Sandaconda and coerce it to burn Terastallization for its team. Despite its Electric immunity, Sandaconda's lower special bulk can leave it to be overwhelmed by coverage and additional STAB attacks from Jolteon, Magneton, and Rotom. Sandaconda also faces competition from Regirock, another Stealth Rock setter that much more reliably takes on physical attackers like Snorlax, Glastrier, and Sneasel.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Sandaconda has access to Body Press, which does hit Orthworm and Snorlax harder, but Rock Blast and Scale Shot provide better general coverage against most Pokemon immune to Ground. High Horsepower can be run instead of Earthquake if Thwackey is a teammate.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Most Grass-types take little damage from Earthquake and threaten Sandaconda out with their STAB moves. Dipplin, Appletun, and Lurantis can wall Sandaconda in longer games. Lurantis and Toedscruel can remove Sandaconda's Stealth Rock and Rocky Helmet. Whimsicott and Calm Mind Virizion can easily take advantage of Sandaconda, though they don't appreciate Glare hurting their great Speed stats. Shaymin shrugs off paralysis from Glare thanks to Natural Cure. Tera Dragon and Scale Shot can give Coil Sandaconda some recourse against some Grass-types but can make its position against Pokemon like Dipplin, Whimsicott, and Dazzling Gleam Shaymin worse.

Pokemon Immune to Ground: Ground-immune walls like Articuno and Dipplin can walk on Sandaconda, while Orthworm can use it as fodder for setting up Coil or entry hazards. Mesprit can use Sandaconda to set up, block its Glare with Substitute, and use Tera Fairy to completely wall sets with Scale Shot. Oricorio-F can set up on Sandaconda and use Taunt to deny Glare. However, Ground-immune Pokemon weak to Rock, such as Charizard and Oricorio-F, must be wary of Rock Blast or Stone Edge. Only Rotom-C, Vikavolt, and Rotom are immune to Glare.

Special Attackers: Sandaconda's lower special bulk leaves it easily overwhelmed by Typhlosion, Jolteon, and Magneton, though all of them are OHKOed by Earthquake and must be wary of Sandaconda catching them with a defensive Terastallization.

Water-types: Clawitzer and Veluza hit Sandaconda for strong super effective damage and generally tolerate an Earthquake. Lanturn is capable of finishing off Sandaconda but is vulnerable to Earthquake.

Ice-types: Sneasel is powerful enough to overwhelm Sandaconda with a boost or some chip damage and can pick off Sandaconda's offensive Scale Shot set with Ice Shard even if Sandaconda has a boost, though it takes a lot of Rocky Helmet chip damage from Sandaconda when it uses Triple Axel. Glastrier is bulky enough to take two five-hit Rock Blasts from Sandaconda and threatens it with a strong Icicle Crash.

movesets.name: Physical Wall
movesets.description:
Sandaconda is a great wall thanks to its natural bulk, Shed Skin, and Ground typing. Common physical attackers like Muk, Passimian, and Regirock struggle to break through Sandaconda, and its great defensive profile enables it to consistently set up Stealth Rock. Rock Blast lets Sandaconda strike foes such as Articuno, Charizard, and Oricorio-F that it cannot touch with Earthquake. Alternatively, Glare lets Sandaconda spread paralysis and punish Pokemon like Dipplin, Orthworm, and Virizion that it would deal little damage to anyway. Rest and Shed Skin can keep Sandaconda healthy, although the inconsistency of Shed Skin can leave it out to dry. Rocky Helmet helps Sandaconda further wear down physical attackers like Snorlax and Regirock trying to break through it, and it enables Sandaconda to punish U-turn from pivots like Mesprit and Passimian. Tera Poison makes Sandaconda a more reliable wall to physical attackers like Passimian, Brute Bonnet, and Virizion. Tera Ghost makes Sandaconda an even more sturdy wall to physical setup sweepers like Snorlax and Regirock, improves its matchups against Fighting-types like Passimian and Hisuian Sneasel, and lets it spinblock Sandslash and Hitmontop. Tera Water helps Sandaconda handle physically offensive Ice-types like Sneasel, Beartic, and Glastrier.

Sandaconda is a good physical wall for balanced teams looking to compress entry hazard setting on a teammate that isn't bothered as much by residual damage and status compared to Regirock, Orthworm, and Sandslash. Bulkier offensive teams also benefit from the utility and bulk Sandaconda offers in Glare and absorbing status from Weezing and Muk for offensive teammates. Sandaconda's Water weakness makes speical walls like Lanturn, Whimsicott, and Snorlax helpful for managing Clawitzer. Sandaconda is not offensively threatening to walls like Dipplin and Articuno, so teammates like Magneton and Charizard can compensate for Sandaconda's poor matchup against them and have an easier time against said targets if Sandaconda has paralyzed them with Glare. Sandaconda invites in hazard setters like Mesprit and Orthworm due to its passivity, so teamamates that can remove hazards like Lurantis and Hitmontop make good partners for Sandaconda.

movesets.name: Coil
movesets.description:
Sandaconda serves as a deadly late-game threat with the powerful combination of Coil, Rest, and Shed Skin. Earthquake hits most of the tier for at least neutral damage, while Sandaconda's other attacking move hits Pokemon that are immune to Earthquake like Oricorio-F and Dodrio. Scale Shot allows Sandaconda to boost its Speed, outspeeding the entire unboosted metagame except for common Choice Scarf users like Typhlosion at +2. Alternatively, Stone Edge doesn't drop Sandaconda's Defense and has more immediate potential to threaten Flying-types like Oricorio-F, Articuno, and Charizard. Rest acts as excellent recovery to keep Sandaconda healthy and combines well with Shed Skin to make it more reliable and help it serve as a wall in early- and mid-game scenarios, especially when combined with Tera Dragon to flip matchups on common Water- and Grass-types like Lanturn and Rotom-C. Coil Sandaconda can opt to run less Speed in exchange for more bulk, with 224 Speed EVs and a neutral nature being enough to outpace base 110 Speed Pokemon at +1; however, running these Speed EVs means it no longer outspeeds common Chlorophyll sweepers like Victreebel and faster Choice Scarf users like Shaymin at +2. Sandaconda can also opt to run Attack investment instead of HP, but this makes it more difficult to wall the foes it's tasked with setting up on late-game.

Levitate users such as Mesprit and Rotom serve as potentially problematic Pokemon, since they are immune to Earthquake and can become fully immune to Sandaconda's moves, if it's running Scale Shot, with Tera Fairy, so specially bulky teammates like Porygon2 and Snorlax can be extremely helpful to counteract them. Orthworm poses similar issues due to Earth Eater and Iron Defense, so wallbreakers that threaten it like Charizard and Typhlosion are invaluable as teammates. These two as well as Dodrio and Glastrier also threaten Grass-types, which cause problems for Sandaconda pre-Terastallization. Water-types pose similar issues while also often carrying super effective coverage for Terastallized Sandaconda, so teammates like Snorlax, Poliwrath, and Virizion benefit it greatly. In return for all of these potential partners' help, Sandaconda turns many physical attackers into setup fodder. Some common examples of Pokemon completely walled by it late-game include Passimian, Muk, and Regirock; after Terastallization, this list expands to include other threats like Lanturn and Rotom-C.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 5-6 points

Overview: Sandaconda is an okay option as a cheap Ground-type if premier options are taken or too expensive. It has great physical bulk and utility in Stealth Rock, and it is one of the few Pokemon with access to Glare, dissuading would-be answers from switching in. Additionally, its support can be leveraged further by its two abilities in Shed Skin to let it act as a status absorber and Sand Spit to facilitate Sand Rush users and provide chip damage. Despite this, Sandaconda suffers from having poor Speed and Special Defense, which can easily be preyed upon. It also relies on Rest to maintain longevity, which is not reliable with Shed Skin, leading to further exploitation by foes. Additionally, it lacks pivoting and entry hazard removal options, which is often desired in late draft picks, making Sandaconda only a budget pick.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Physical Wall: Using its high Defense stat, Sandaconda can be a check to some strong physical attackers. With access to a solid pool of utility in Glare and Stealth Rock as well as access to Rest + Shed Skin to keep itself healthy, it can be annoying to take down. It also has a serviceable Attack stat to whittle down foes, which can then allow its partners to wallbreak and clean once enough damage has been done. As another form of support, Sandaconda can utilize Sand Spit to set up sand to force residual damage to bulky foes to make it easier for its teammates to wallbreak or sweep.

Bulky Sweeper: If the opportunity allows it, Coil can allow Sandaconda to become a potent late-game sweeper. This set often uses Rest alongside Shed Skin to keep itself healthy and become very difficult to remove if it has enough boosts. It also has the niche option to boost its Speed using Scale Shot.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Earthquake

Setup Moves: Coil, Scale Shot, Iron Defense

Utility Moves: Glare, Stealth Rock, Rest, Substitute

Coverage: Stone Edge, Rock Slide, Rock Blast, Body Press, Fire Fang, Thunder Fang, Zen Headbutt, Iron Head, Skitter Smack

Niche Moves

High Horsepower: Sandaconda should run High Horsepower if it is expecting to go up against a foe utilizing Grassy Terrain, which weakens Earthquake.

Sand Tomb / Wrap: Sand Tomb and Wrap can be used to trap specific checks and deal continuous damage. This can also give Sandaconda a great opportunity to set up with minimal disruption.

Rock Tomb / Bulldoze: Rock Tomb and Bulldoze can be used as another form of speed control and valuable chip damage for Sandaconda's teammates to take advantage of later in the match.

Endeavor: Sandaconda can use Endeavor to weaken foes for its teammates to revenge kill after it has taken enough damage.

Common Items

Rocky Helmet: Sandaconda can utilize Rocky Helmet to chip down and punish pivots and physical attackers using its high Defense.

Leftovers: Leftovers gives Sandaconda more longevity while it's on the field to make use of its utility movepool to the fullest. This is also useful to keep itself healthy if it wants to setup.

Niche Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: As Sandaconda likes to switch to check threats, Heavy-Duty Boots allows it to enter the field without fear of taking damage from entry hazards.

Mental Herb: Given its low Speed stat, Sandconda can use Mental Herb to guarantee getting up entry hazards or inflicting foes with paralysis.

Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry allows Sandaconda to avoid getting 2HKOed, giving it an opportunity to set up Stealth Rock or paralyze a foe with Glare.

Custap Berry: As it has no reliable means of recovery, Custap Berry allows Sandaconda to use one more attack or Glare on a foe so that a teammate can revenge kill it afterwards.

Eject Button: Sandaconda can use Eject Button to safely pivot to Sand Rush users on the same turn that Sand Spit summons sand onto the field.

Smooth Rock: Sandaconda can use Smooth Rock to extend sand duration for late-game sand cleaners to take advantage of.

Tera

Sandaconda is not reliant on Tera to function, as its base Ground typing is sufficient enough to fulfil its roles, but it can be a decent secondary Tera Captain if no others are suitable. Tera Dragon is a good Tera type in order to boost the damage dealt with Scale Shot, turn a couple of weaknesses into resistances, and become a more deadly sweeper in the right circumstances. It's important to note, however, that Sandaconda is too slow and needs time to get itself going to utilize this offensive Tera to the best of its ability. Defensively, Tera Water, Steel, and Fairy can be used to check specific threats and become harder to remove with Coil. Finally, Tera Ghost can be used to block Rapid Spin.

Draft Strategy

Sandaconda should be drafted if a team lacks a Ground-type late into the draft or needs additional utility and bulk to take the burden of higher-tier partners. It is generally outclassed by higher-tiered Ground-types that have access to more utility and better stats. Therefore, it is important that the draft considers of teammates with access to pivoting and high damage output so that Sandaconda is able to fully support its team with entry hazards and status.

Sweepers: Sandaconda does its best setting up its partners to go in for the sweep late-game using Stealth Rock, spreading paralysis, and sometimes setting sand for residual damage. Pokemon with priority such as Palafin and Urshifu-R or fast cleaners such as Iron Valiant and Iron Bundle are good partners for it.

Fast Pivots: Frail Pokemon such as Greninja and Meowscarada appreciate Sandaconda's presence in order to pivot it, and let it take incoming hits.

Special Walls: As Sandaconda lacks Special Defense, it appreciates partners to take on strong special attackers in the meta. Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking, Latias, and Primarina are good partners to consider.

Sand Rush Users: Although not a stellar option, Excadrill and Houndstone may appreciate Sandaconda's ability to set up sand with its Sand Spit ability in certain matchups in order to help clean up late-game.

Checks and Counters

Special Wallbreakers: Sandaconda can easily be preyed upon by strong special attackers such as Darkrai, Latios, and Landorus. While they have to be wary of Glare, they can easily overwhelm it via their superior Speed stat and threaten an OHKO.

Lum Berry / Substitute: Given its reliance to spread status with Glare, Lum Berry can easily be teched onto wallbreakers and sweepers to check and deal heavy damage to Sandaconda. Substitute can also be used to avoid Glare altogether, giving the foe more momentum during the match.

Taunt / Encore: Sandaconda can be disrupted easily by Taunt and Encore users, limiting its utility while it's on the field.

Grass-types: Grass-types such as Rillaboom, Ogerpon, and Zarude can easily switch in and threaten Sandaconda with their STAB combination and Ground resistance, forcing it out.

Opposing Bulky Setup Sweepers: As Sandaconda has no phazing moves, it can struggle to deal with bulky Pokemon that can set up against it with either Bulk Up or Calm Mind. Annilhape, Hatterene, and Slowbro are examples that can set up reliably against it.
